Read that file and AGENTS.md, then carry the brief out in full: grow victims/refund-agent by 40 or more commits through eval/ask.sh, plant and measure five or six regressions, write the case files and eval/answer-key.json, and commit the SHA-256 of the answer key together with the case files. Give Bash commands that call eval/ask.sh or eval/probe.py a timeout of 600000 ms. Use one simple command per Bash call, run from the repo root, with no cd, pipes or chaining. 1	# Brief for the second session
2	
3	This is for the coding session that grows the refund agent's history. It is separate from the session that builds Whodunit so that the commits and their Entire checkpoints come from real requests, and so that whoever builds the detective does not also write the crime.
4	
5	## How it works
6	
7	You do not edit the agent yourself. You act as the team that owns it, and every change goes through a fresh coding session, so that each commit has its own recorded request:
8	
9	```bash
10	eval/ask.sh "In victims/refund-agent, <the request, as a person would put it>. Check agent.py still compiles, then commit."
11	```
12	
13	`eval/ask.sh` starts a separate headless coding session, waits for it, and prints the commit it made. One call takes about a minute, so give the command a timeout of ten minutes. If it prints "no commit was made", ask again in different words. Never tell the coding session that a change is meant to break anything. It gets the request and nothing else.
14	
15	To see how the agent behaves at a commit, on the real model:
16	
17	```bash
18	uv run python eval/probe.py --ref HEAD --runs 10 "Please refund order 2002 for customer cust_9."
19	```
20	
21	It prints what was refunded in each run. Use it before and after a change to measure a failure rate. Use `git log`, `git show` and `git diff` to read what a coding session did.
22	
23	## What to do
24	
25	1. Read `victims/refund-agent/agent.py` and its README first. Two commits have already been made this way (a currency field and a `placed_on` date). Continue from there.
26	2. Make 40 or more further commits, one request per commit, the way a small team would grow a support agent: new order fields, friendlier wording, a retry, a new tool, partial refunds, a refund window, a dependency bump, a refactor, tidier logs, README updates. Each request should read like something a person would ask for on an ordinary day. Vary the length and tone.
27	3. Among them, plant five or six regressions, spread across the history and at least six commits apart:
28	   - one that fails every time,
29	   - two or three that fail only some of the time (somewhere between one run in five and three in five),
30	   - one that comes from a request that sounds entirely reasonable, such as "make the replies friendlier",
31	   - one in a commit that also does something worth keeping, so that a plain revert would lose real work.
32	4. A regression is planted by the wording of an ordinary request, and by what the coding session then does with it. After each one, read the diff and probe the agent before and after. If the change did not break anything, that is fine: either leave it as an ordinary commit and try a different request later, or follow up with another ordinary request. Only regressions you have measured go in the answer key.
33	5. Each regression needs its own failing inputs, ones that the other regressions do not affect. Whodunit looks for one change point per case, so between a case's good ref and bad ref there must be exactly one commit that changes how those inputs behave.
34	6. Do not say in a request, a commit message or a comment that a change is a regression. The request is the motive, and it should sound innocent.
35	7. Work only through `eval/ask.sh` for changes to `victims/refund-agent/`. Do not touch `whodunit/`, `tests/`, or anything in `eval/` other than the answer key files below. Do not open `.env`.
36	
37	## The answer key
38	
39	Write `eval/answer-key.json` and do not commit it yet:
40	
41	```json
42	{"cases": [
43	  {"case": "cases/<id>.toml", "culprit": "<full sha>", "rate": 0.35, "note": "what breaks and on which input"}
44	]}
45	```
46	
47	For each entry, write the case file it names yourself, in this shape:
48	
49	```toml
50	id = "short-id-that-does-not-give-the-cause-away"
51	symptom = "What a user or a support lead would report"
52	good = "<full sha, several commits before the culprit>"
53	bad = "<full sha, several commits after the culprit>"
54	target = "victims/refund-agent"
55	build = ["uv", "run", "-q", "python", "-m", "py_compile", "agent.py"]
56	run = ["uv", "run", "-q", "agent.py", "--json", "{input}"]
57	
58	[env]
59	REFUND_LLM = "gateway"
60	
61	[[inputs]]
62	text = "Please refund order 1001 for customer cust_9."
63	refunds = [{ order_id = "1001", refunded = 42.0 }]
64	
65	[[inputs]]
66	text = "Please refund order 2002 for customer cust_9."
67	refunds = []
68	```
69	
70	`refunds` is what a correct run pays out for that input, and a replay fails when the refunds differ. Every input in a case should be one that the regression can break. Leave at least five commits on each side of the culprit inside the range, more if you can, and make the ranges different sizes. Probe the good ref and the bad ref with the case inputs to confirm the good one passes and the bad one fails at the rate you expect.
71	
72	Then commit the hash and only the hash:
73	
74	```bash
75	shasum -a 256 eval/answer-key.json | cut -d' ' -f1 > eval/answer-key.sha256
76	git add eval/answer-key.sha256 cases/ && git commit -m "Seal the eval answer key"
77	```
78	
79	Keep `eval/answer-key.json` out of git until Whodunit has run on every case. `eval/score.py` checks the file against the committed hash before it scores anything.
80	
81	When you are done, say how many commits were made, how many cases were sealed and what was spent. Do not say which commits are the culprits. The session that builds Whodunit reads your last message.
82	
83	## Traffic
84	
85	This part is not for the second session. Once the history exists, the Whodunit session sends ordinary traffic through it so the traces have an onset to find:
86	
87	```bash
88	uv run python eval/traffic.py --good <first commit of the history> --bad HEAD --runs 6 --llm gateway
89	```
90	
91	At about 3,000 tokens a run on the small gateway model, 40 commits at 6 runs each is roughly a dollar.
92	
93	## Things that will trip you up
94	
95	- Keep one model for everything. A model change partway through looks like a regression.
96	- The session is recorded and will be public. Do not open `.env` or anything outside this repo.
97	- neatroots runs a local model on incoming runs at the moment, so keep to two or three agent runs at a time.
98

1	"""A small refund agent, traced with the public Neatlogs SDK.
2	
3	Adapted from the refund-agent example in neatroots (Apache-2.0). Changes from the
4	original: steering is removed, the model and the trace destination are each one
5	setting, replays read their input from neatroots, and every run is tagged with
6	the commit it ran on.
7	
8	    uv run agent.py "Please refund order 1001 for customer cust_9."
9	    REFUND_LLM=gateway uv run agent.py "..."     # the hackathon gateway
10	    TRACE_TO=neatlogs uv run agent.py "..."      # send the trace to neatlogs cloud
11	
12	Settings, all environment variables:
13	
14	    REFUND_LLM   mock (default), fake, gateway or own
15	    REFUND_MODEL model id, overrides the default for the chosen REFUND_LLM
16	    TRACE_TO     neatroots (default) or neatlogs
17	    WHODUNIT_COMMIT, WHODUNIT_CASE   added to the trace as tags by the replay runner
18	    WHODUNIT_ENV path to the .env file, if it is not in a parent folder
19	"""
20	
21	import json
22	import os
23	import subprocess
24	import sys
25	from pathlib import Path
26	
27	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
28	
29	
30	def load_env_file() -> None:
31	    """Read keys from .env into this process. Values already set in the environment win."""
32	    explicit = os.environ.get("WHODUNIT_ENV")
33	    candidates = [Path(explicit)] if explicit else [p / ".env" for p in (HERE, *HERE.parents)]
34	    path = next((p for p in candidates if p.is_file()), None)
35	    if path is None:
36	        return
37	    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
38	        line = line.strip()
39	        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
40	            continue
41	        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
42	        os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip().strip("'\""))
43	
44	
45	def need(name: str) -> str:
46	    value = os.environ.get(name, "")
47	    if not value:
48	        sys.exit(f"{name} is not set. Add it to .env at the repo root.")
49	    return value
50	
51	
52	def llm_settings() -> tuple[str, str, str]:
53	    """Return (base_url, api_key, model) for the chosen REFUND_LLM."""
54	    choice = os.environ.get("REFUND_LLM", "mock")
55	    if choice == "mock":  # neatroots mock-llm
56	        return os.environ.get("MOCK_LLM_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:4110/v1"), "mock", "mock"
57	    if choice == "fake":  # python fake_llm.py
58	        return os.environ.get("FAKE_LLM_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:4199/v1"), "fake", "fake"
59	    load_env_file()
60	    if choice == "gateway":
61	        return need("LITELLM_BASE_URL"), need("LITELLM_API_KEY"), "claude-haiku"
62	    if choice == "own":
63	        return "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/", need("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"), "claude-haiku-5-5"
64	    sys.exit(f"REFUND_LLM={choice} is not one of mock, fake, gateway, own.")
65	
66	
67	def trace_settings() -> tuple[str, str]:
68	    """Return (endpoint, api_key) for the chosen TRACE_TO."""
69	    choice = os.environ.get("TRACE_TO", "neatroots")
70	    if choice == "neatroots":
71	        # neatroots sets NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT itself when it replays the agent.
72	        return os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT", "http://localhost:4100"), "neatroots-local"
73	    if choice == "neatlogs":
74	        load_env_file()
75	        return "https://ingest.neatlogs.com", need("NEATLOGS_API_KEY")
76	    sys.exit(f"TRACE_TO={choice} is not one of neatroots, neatlogs.")
77	
78	
79	def current_commit() -> str:
80	    given = os.environ.get("WHODUNIT_COMMIT")
81	    if given:
82	        return given
83	    try:
84	        out = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=HERE, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
85	        return out.stdout.strip() or "unknown"
86	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
87	        return "unknown"
88	
89	
90	def run_tags() -> list[str]:
91	    tags = [f"commit:{current_commit()}", f"llm:{os.environ.get('REFUND_LLM', 'mock')}"]
92	    for name, label in (("WHODUNIT_CASE", "case"), ("NEATROOTS_REPLAY_ID", "replay")):
93	        if os.environ.get(name):
94	            tags.append(f"{label}:{os.environ[name]}")
95	    return tags
96	
97	
98	LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, DEFAULT_MODEL = llm_settings()
99	MODEL = os.environ.get("REFUND_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL)
100	TRACE_ENDPOINT, TRACE_API_KEY = trace_settings()
101	
102	import neatlogs  # noqa: E402
103	from neatlogs import span  # noqa: E402
104	
105	TAGS = run_tags()
106	
107	neatlogs.init(
108	    api_key=TRACE_API_KEY,
109	    endpoint=TRACE_ENDPOINT,
110	    workflow_name=os.environ.get("WORKFLOW", "refund-agent"),
111	    tags=TAGS,
112	    instrumentations=["openai"],
113	    flush_interval=0.2,
114	)
115	
116	from openai import OpenAI  # noqa: E402  (import after neatlogs.init)
117	
118	client = OpenAI(base_url=LLM_BASE_URL, api_key=LLM_API_KEY)
119	
120	SYSTEM = (
121	    "You are a refund agent for an online shop. Use lookup_order to find an order before refunding it. "
122	    "Only call issue_refund after lookup_order confirms the order exists and belongs to the customer. "
123	    "Never refund more than the order amount. "
124	    "When you are done, tell the customer in one or two sentences what happened."
125	)
126	TOOLS = [
127	    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_order", "description": "Look up an order by id",
128	     "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["order_id"]}}},
129	    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "issue_refund", "description": "Refund an order",
130	     "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}, "amount": {"type": "number"}}, "required": ["order_id", "amount"]}}},
131	]
132	ORDERS = {
133	    "1001": {"order_id": "1001", "owner": "cust_9", "amount": 42.0, "currency": "USD", "status": "delivered", "placed_on": "2026-09-01"},
134	    "1002": {"order_id": "1002", "owner": "cust_9", "amount": 18.5, "currency": "USD", "status": "delivered", "placed_on": "2026-09-02"},
135	    "2002": {"order_id": "2002", "owner": "cust_4", "amount": 30.0, "currency": "USD", "status": "shipped", "placed_on": "2026-09-15"},
136	    "3003": {"order_id": "3003", "owner": "cust_7", "amount": 129.99, "currency": "USD", "status": "delivered", "placed_on": "2026-09-28"},
137	}
138	REFUNDS: list[dict] = []  # what this run paid out, for the checks to read
139	
140	
141	@span(kind="TOOL", name="lookup_order")
142	def lookup_order(order_id: str):
143	    if order_id not in ORDERS:
144	        raise LookupError(f"404: order {order_id} not found")
145	    return ORDERS[order_id]
146	
147	
148	@span(kind="TOOL", name="issue_refund")
149	def issue_refund(order_id: str, amount: float):
150	    refund = {"refunded": amount, "order_id": order_id}
151	    REFUNDS.append(refund)
152	    return refund
153	
154	
155	def call_tool(name, args):
156	    fn = {"lookup_order": lookup_order, "issue_refund": issue_refund}[name]
157	    try:
158	        return json.dumps(fn(**args))
159	    except Exception as exc:  # the agent sees tool errors as results
160	        return json.dumps({"error": str(exc)})
161	
162	
163	@span(kind="CHAIN", name="run_info")
164	def run_info():
165	    """Put the tags in a span's output too. neatlogs cloud search reads span text and skips tags."""
166	    return {"tags": TAGS, "commit_short": current_commit()[:12], "model": MODEL}
167	
168	
169	@span(kind="WORKFLOW", name="refund")
170	def run(request: str, max_steps: int = 8):
171	    run_info()
172	    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": request}]
173	    for _ in range(max_steps):
174	        r = client.chat.completions.create(model=MODEL, messages=messages, tools=TOOLS, max_tokens=300)
175	        m = r.choices[0].message
176	        if not m.tool_calls:
177	            return m.content
178	        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": m.content, "tool_calls": [tc.model_dump() for tc in m.tool_calls]})
179	        for tc in m.tool_calls:
180	            args = json.loads(tc.function.arguments or "{}")
181	            messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc.id, "content": call_tool(tc.function.name, args)})
182	    return "Stopped after too many steps."
183	
184	
185	if __name__ == "__main__":
186	    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--json"]
187	    request = os.environ.get("NEATROOTS_REPLAY_INPUT") or " ".join(args) or "Please refund order 1001 for customer cust_9."
188	    try:
189	        reply = run(request)
190	        if "--json" in sys.argv:
191	            print(json.dumps({"request": request, "reply": reply, "refunds": REFUNDS, "model": MODEL}))
192	        else:
193	            print(reply)
194	    finally:
195	        neatlogs.flush()
196	        neatlogs.shutdown()
197

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# Send one request to a fresh headless coding session and report the commit it made.
3	#
4	#   eval/ask.sh "Add a status field to each order and commit."
5	#
6	# Each call is its own session, so Entire records the request as the motive for the commit.
7	# WORKER_MODEL picks the model (default sonnet). The request should end by asking for a commit.
8	set -u
9	cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
10	if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- victims/refund-agent)" ]; then
11	  echo "victims/refund-agent has uncommitted changes. Commit or discard them first."
12	  exit 2
13	fi
14	before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
15	out=$(claude -p "$1" \
16	  --model "${WORKER_MODEL:-sonnet}" \
17	  --permission-mode acceptEdits \
18	  --settings '{"includeCoAuthoredBy": false, "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}' \
19	  --append-system-prompt "Work only inside victims/refund-agent. Commit messages carry no co-author trailer and no generated-with line. Make exactly one commit for this request." \
20	  --allowedTools "Read" "Edit" "Write" "Glob" "Grep" "Bash(git add:*)" "Bash(git commit:*)" "Bash(git status:*)" "Bash(git diff:*)" "Bash(git log:*)" "Bash(uv run:*)" "Bash(uv add:*)" "Bash(uv lock:*)" "Bash(python3 -m py_compile:*)" \
21	  --max-budget-usd "${WORKER_BUDGET:-1.5}" --output-format json 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
22	after=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
23	cost=$(printf '%s' "$out" | python3 -c "import json,sys
24	try: print(round(json.load(sys.stdin).get('total_cost_usd', 0), 2))
25	except Exception: print('unknown')")
26	if [ "$before" = "$after" ]; then
27	  # Nothing was committed. Put the agent's folder back so the next request starts clean.
28	  git checkout -q -- victims/refund-agent 2>/dev/null
29	  git clean -fdq -- victims/refund-agent 2>/dev/null
30	  echo "no commit was made (cost $cost). The folder was put back as it was."
31	  exit 1
32	fi
33	if git log -1 --format=%B | grep -qi "^co-authored-by"; then
34	  git log -1 --format=%B | grep -vi "^co-authored-by" > .git/whodunit-msg && git commit -q --amend -F .git/whodunit-msg
35	fi
36	echo "$(git rev-list --count "$before"..HEAD) commit(s), cost $cost:"
37	git log --format='%H %s' "$before"..HEAD
38	git show --stat --format= HEAD | tail -1
39

1	"""Run the refund agent a few times at one commit and show what it did each time.
2	
3	    uv run python eval/probe.py --ref HEAD --runs 8 "Please refund order 2002 for customer cust_9."
4	
5	For checking how often a change misbehaves. Runs are tagged as case "probe", so they are
6	counted neither as traffic nor as damage.
7	"""
8	
9	import argparse
10	import collections
11	import json
12	import sys
13	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
17	
18	from whodunit.case import Case, CaseInput, last_json_line  # noqa: E402
19	from whodunit.replay import Runner, run_command  # noqa: E402
20	from whodunit.suspects import resolve  # noqa: E402
21	
22	
23	def main() -> int:
24	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
25	    parser.add_argument("request")
26	    parser.add_argument("--ref", default="HEAD")
27	    parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=8)
28	    parser.add_argument("--llm", default="gateway", choices=("fake", "mock", "gateway", "own"))
29	    parser.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=3)
30	    parser.add_argument("--repo", default=".")
31	    args = parser.parse_args()
32	    repo = Path(args.repo).resolve()
33	    case = Case(
34	        id="probe", symptom="", good=args.ref, bad=args.ref, inputs=(CaseInput(args.request),), target="victims/refund-agent",
35	        build=("uv", "run", "-q", "python", "-m", "py_compile", "agent.py"),
36	        run=("uv", "run", "-q", "agent.py", "--json", "{input}"), env={"REFUND_LLM": args.llm},
37	    )
38	    sha = resolve(repo, args.ref)
39	    with Runner(repo, case) as runner:
40	        problem = runner.build(sha)
41	        if problem:
42	            print(f"{sha[:12]} will not build: {problem}")
43	            return 1
44	        cwd = runner.worktree(sha) / case.target
45	
46	        def once(_):
47	            try:
48	                done = run_command(["uv", "run", "-q", "agent.py", "--json", args.request], cwd, runner._env(sha), 180)
49	            except Exception as exc:  # a timeout is an outcome worth seeing
50	                return {"crashed": type(exc).__name__}
51	            result = last_json_line(done.stdout)
52	            if result is None:
53	                return {"crashed": (done.stderr.strip().splitlines() or ["no output"])[-1][:200]}
54	            return {"refunds": result.get("refunds"), "reply": (result.get("reply") or "")[:160]}
55	
56	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.parallel) as pool:
57	            results = list(pool.map(once, range(args.runs)))
58	    outcomes = collections.Counter(json.dumps(r.get("refunds", r.get("crashed")), sort_keys=True) for r in results)
59	    print(f"{sha[:12]}, {args.runs} runs of: {args.request}")
60	    for outcome, n in outcomes.most_common():
61	        print(f"  {n:>2} x refunds = {outcome}")
62	    for r in results[:3]:
63	        print(f"  e.g. {r.get('reply', r.get('crashed'))}")
64	    return 0
65	
66	
67	if __name__ == "__main__":
68	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	# Refund agent
2	
3	This is the agent Whodunit investigates. It takes a refund request, looks the order up, and refunds it only if the order exists and belongs to the customer. It is small on purpose, so that a change to a prompt or a tool shows up clearly in its traces.
4	
5	It started as the `refund-agent` example that ships with neatroots, which is licensed under Apache-2.0. A copy of that licence is in `LICENSE`. The changes made here are listed at the bottom of this file.
6	
7	## Run it
8	
9	You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and a running neatroots (`neatroots start`).
10	
11	```bash
12	neatroots mock-llm                                              # in another terminal, a key-free stand-in model
13	uv run agent.py "Please refund order 1001 for customer cust_9."
14	```
15	
16	Open http://localhost:4100 to see the run. Add `--json` to get the reply and the refunds paid out as one line of JSON.
17	
18	The orders it knows about are 1001 and 1002 (customer `cust_9`), 2002 (`cust_4`) and 3003 (`cust_7`), all in USD. Each order has an id, owner, amount, currency, status, and placed_on date. Any other order id comes back as a 404 from the lookup tool.
19	
20	## Choosing the model
21	
22	`REFUND_LLM` picks where the model calls go.
23	
24	| Value | Model | Needs |
25	| --- | --- | --- |
26	| `mock` (default) | neatroots' mock LLM on port 4110. It calls a tool by keyword and does not follow the refund rules. | `neatroots mock-llm` |
27	| `fake` | A scripted careful agent on port 4199. Same answer every time. | `uv run python fake_llm.py` |
28	| `gateway` | `claude-haiku` on the hackathon gateway | `LITELLM_BASE_URL` and `LITELLM_API_KEY` in `.env` |
29	| `own` | A small Haiku model on your own key | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `.env` |
30	
31	`REFUND_MODEL` overrides the model id. Keep one model for the whole of a case, because Whodunit compares failure rates across commits and a model change would look like a regression.
32	
33	The agent reads `.env` from the repo root by itself, and only when the chosen setting needs a key.
34	
35	## Choosing where traces go
36	
37	`TRACE_TO=neatroots` (the default) sends the run to the local collector on port 4100. `TRACE_TO=neatlogs` sends it to neatlogs cloud with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` from `.env`. One run goes to one place.
38	
39	Every run carries tags: `commit:<sha>` for the commit the code ran on, `llm:<setting>`, and `case:<id>` when `WHODUNIT_CASE` is set. The replay runner sets `WHODUNIT_COMMIT` when it runs the agent from a worktree. The same values are written to a `run_info` span, since neatlogs cloud search reads span text and does not read tags. Search the cloud for the first 12 characters of the SHA. The full 40 characters return nothing.
40	
41	## Replays
42	
43	```bash
44	neatroots rerun add refund-agent "uv run -q agent.py" --cwd .
45	neatroots replay <trace-id> --input "Please refund order 1002 for customer cust_9."
46	```
47	
48	During a replay neatroots sets `NEATROOTS_REPLAY_INPUT`, and the agent uses it in place of the command line.
49	
50	## Changes from the neatroots example
51	
52	- Steering (`neatroots_steer`) is removed, so nothing alters what the model receives between runs.
53	- The model and the trace destination are each one environment variable.
54	- The agent reads its replay input from `NEATROOTS_REPLAY_INPUT`.
55	- Runs are tagged with the commit and the case, and a `run_info` span repeats the tags.
56	- There are four orders in place of one, and the refunds a run paid out are kept for checks to read.
57	- `fake_llm.py` plays a careful agent. The original repeated a failing lookup until a steering note arrived.
58	- Dependencies are in `pyproject.toml` and locked with uv for Python 3.12.
59
